'''Michael Louis Friendly''' (born 1945) is a Canadian [[psychologist]], Professor of [[Psychology]] at [[York University]] in Ontario, Canada, and director of its Statistical Consulting Service, especially known for his contributions to graphical methods for categorical and multivariate data, and on the history of [[data visualization|data]] and [[information visualisation]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://www.wiley.com/WileyCDA/WileyTitle/productCd-0471681601.html |title=Visual Statistics: Seeing Data with Dynamic Interactive Graphics |last1=Young |first1=Forrest W. |last2=Valero-Mora |first2=Pedro M. |last3=Friendly |first3=Michael |publisher=Wiley |date=2011 |access-date=February 23, 2021 |archive-date=September 17, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170917234951/http://www.wiley.com/WileyCDA/WileyTitle/productCd-0471681601.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>Rosenberg, Daniel, and Anthony Grafton. ''Cartographies of time: A history of the timeline.'' Princeton Architectural Press, 2013.</ref>



== Biography ==
Born in [[New York City]], Friendly obtained his BS in 1966 from the [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]], and his MS in 1969 from [[Princeton University]]. In 1971/2 he also obtained his PhD in psychology at Princeton under supervision of [[Harold Gulliksen]] and Peter Ornstein, with the thesis titled "Proximity Analysis and the Structure of Organization in Free Recall."<ref>Friendly, Michael L. "[http://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED062373.pdf Proximity Analysis and the Structure of Organization in Free Recall.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170314195653/http://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED062373.pdf |date=March 14, 2017 }}" (1972).</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=72941}}</ref>

Friendly's first research project in the field of [[psychometrics]] and [[cognitive psychology]] had started at the [[Educational Testing Service]] and [[Princeton University]], and was made possible by a Psychometric Fellowship awarded by the Educational Testing Service. After graduation Friendly jointed the Department of Psychology at the [[York University]] in Ontario, Canada, where he continued his research. At the York University he was appointed Associate Professor and later on Professor of Psychology, and since 1985 also director of its Statistical Consulting Service.

Friendly is Associate Editor of the ''Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics'' and an Editor of ''Statistical Science.''
In 2018 he became a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx|title=ASA Fellows List|publisher=[[American Statistical Association]]|access-date=2018-08-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201042456/https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx|archive-date=December 1, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Work ==
Friendly's research interests have developed over years. It started in the 1970s with the application of quantitative and computer methods to problems in [[cognitive psychology]], including the cognitive aspects of extracting information from graphical displays.<ref>[http://portal.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=531806&dl=ACM&coll=portal SAS System for Statistical Graphics, First Edition, 1st edition] ABSTRACT From the Publisher. Retrieved 07 July 2008.</ref> In the 1990s Friendly started focussing on the history of statistics and data visualization, and furthermore graphical methods for data and information visualization.<ref>[http://www.yorku.ca/health/psyc/graduate/history_theory.htm Profiles of Faculty Members in the History and Theory of Psychology Area] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080524072445/http://www.yorku.ca/health/psyc/graduate/history_theory.htm |date=May 24, 2008 }}. Department of Psychology. York University. Retrieved 07 July 2008.</ref>

=== Selected articles and reports ===
* 1991. "Interpreting higher order interactions in loglinear analysis: A picture is worth 1000 words". With John Fox. Tech. rep., Institute for Social Research, York University, Toronto, CA.
* 1992. "Graphical methods for categorical data". In: ''Proceedings of the SAS User's Group International Conference'', 17:1367-1373.
* 1994. [http://datavis.ca/papers/4fold/4fold.pdf "A fourfold display for 2 by 2 by K tables"]. Tech. Rep. 217, York University, Psychology Dept.
* 1994. "Mosaic displays for multi-way contingency tables". In: ''Journal of the American Statistical Association'', 89:190-200.
* 2000. [http://datavis.ca/papers/moshist.pdf "A brief history of the mosaic display."] ''Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics''. 11(1):89-107. URL
* 2000. "The roots and branches of statistical graphics". With Dan Denis. In: ''Journal de la Société Française de Statistique'', 141(4):51-60. (published in 2001).
* 2001/2008. [http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.190.9498&rep=rep1&type=pdf "Milestones in the history of thematic cartography, statistical graphics, and data visualization"], URL ''www.datavis.ca/milestones'' 32 (2001): 13. .<ref name="Milestones">{{Cite web |url=http://www.math.yorku.ca/SCS/Gallery/milestone/milestone.pdf |date=2017-10-29 |title=Archived copy |access-date=July 7, 2008 |archive-date=September 26, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180926124138/http://www.math.yorku.ca/SCS/Gallery/milestone/milestone.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

* 2007. "[http://www.datavis.ca/papers/Maps_Chapter5-ocr.pdf Visualizing nature and society]". With [[Gilles Palsky]]. In: [[James R. Akerman]] and Robert W. Karrow, eds., ''Maps: Finding Our Place in the World'', pp.&nbsp;205–251. Chicago, IL: University of Chicago Press.
* 2007. [http://datavis.ca/papers/jcgs-heplots.pdf "HE plots for Multivariate General Linear Models."] ''Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics'', 16, 421–444.
